title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-03-24

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a landmark early‑’73 Spectrum show highlighted by a monster Truckin'→Spanish Jam sequence and an emotional Sing Me Back Home.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean SBD source with generally crisp balance, only minor early‑show SQ quirks. Musically the concert shines – the second set’s He’s Gone → Truckin’ → massive jam (including a rare Spanish Jam) → a concise Dark Star and a heartfelt Sing Me Back Home are repeatedly praised as top‑tier Dead performances. The first set is solid with strong Box of Rain, Tennessee Jed and Playin’, making this one of the most celebrated Spectrum dates.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ≈4.5 stars; overwhelmingly positive comments on both performance and soundboard quality, with many reviewers calling it a top‑10 or “monster” show.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as clear SBD with crisp balance; a few notes of initial SQ hiccups and occasional low mix on Garcia, but overall very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid and diverse, while the second set delivers a unique jam suite that builds from He's Gone through Truckin', an epic Spanish Jam, a tight Dark Star and culminates in an emotional Sing Me Back Home – praised for its seamless transitions despite the unusually short Dark Star.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Emotional vocal on Sing Me Back Home; notable wah‑wah and western‑flavored guitar tones; occasionally low in the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass fire on Box of Rain, strong interplay with Bill during long jam, described as "on fire" throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides double‑guitar textures on Tennessee Jed and adds solid rhythm/vocal work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's psychedelic jazz fills highlighted in Playin' and other jams; praised for “pure psychedelic jazz” moments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s extended jam with Phil lauded as a “great long Phil and Bill jam”; overall drumming described as “playing like a young God.”
